rules.title: Tenant Protection Act - Just Cause for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered rental units must have a legally recognized 'just cause' reason to end a tenancy after a tenant has lived there 12 months. For no-fault terminations (such as owner move-in, withdrawal from rental market, or substantial remodel), the landlord must pay the tenant one month's rent as relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies for which just cause is required to terminate under subdivision (a); covers at-fault just cause (e.g., nonpayment, lease violation) and no-fault just cause (e.g., owner/family move-in, withdrawal from market, demolition/substantial remodel).
rules.penalty: If a tenant fails to vacate after expiration of the termination notice, the relocation assistance or rent waiver amount is recoverable as damages in an action to recover possession.
rules.quoted_span:
the tenancy under subdivision (a), if an owner of residential real property issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause described in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), the owner shall, regardless of the tenant’s income, at the owner’s option, do one of the following:
(A) Assist the tenant to relocate by providing a direct payment to the tenant as described in paragraph (3).

rules.conflict_note: State law yields to stricter local just-cause/rent-control ordinances (e.g., LA RSO/JCO, San Diego, Santa Ana) which impose additional or different requirements; exemptions and unit coverage are detailed elsewhere in Civ. Code § 1947.12/1946.2 not fully quoted in this passage.
